title.value: Unlocking the Potential of Knowledge Distillation: The Role of Teacher Calibration

abstract.value: Knowledge distillation (KD) is one of the successful deep learning compression methods for edge devices, transferring the knowledge from a large model, known as the *teacher*, to a smaller model, referred to as the *student*. KD has demonstrated remarkable performance since its first introduction. However, recent research in KD reveals that using a higher-performance teacher network does not guarantee better performance of the student network. This naturally leads to a question about the criterion for choosing an appropriate teacher. In this paper, we reveal that there is a strong correlation between the calibration error of the teacher and the accuracy of the student. Therefore, we claim that the calibration error of the teacher model can be a selection criterion for knowledge distillation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the performance of KD can be improved by simply applying a temperature-based calibration method that reduces the teacher's calibration error. Our algorithm can be easily applied to other methods, and when applied on top of the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) model, it achieves a new SOTA performance.
